items.stem: What is the role of a sensor?
options: To switch devices on and off
To measure a physical property and send the reading to the computer
To decide what action to take
items.answer: To measure a physical property and send the reading to the computer
items.markingKey: Sensors measure properties such as temperature or light; they do not make decisions.

items.stem: Explain why a sensor alone does not control a device.
items.answer: The sensor only measures and sends data; the microprocessor compares the data with stored values and sends signals to an actuator, which carries out the action.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sensor only measures; 1 mark: processor decides/actuator acts [2]

items.stem: Describe the difference between a monitoring system and a control system, giving an example of each.
items.answer: Monitoring: readings collected and displayed/warnings sounded but no action on the process, e.g. patient monitoring in a hospital. Control: processor uses actuators to change the process, e.g. greenhouse heating.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each description; 1 mark each example [4]

items.stem: Which sensor is most suitable for a greenhouse heater?
items.answer: thermistor/temperature sensor
items.markingKey: A greenhouse heater needs to measure temperature: thermistor/temperature sensor.

items.stem: Palm Grove Hotel in Seoul is installing a street lighting. Identify a suitable sensor and actuator and describe how the system works.
items.answer: Sensor: light sensor (photoresistor); actuator: lamp. The sensor sends readings (via an ADC) to the microprocessor, which compares them with a pre-set value and switches the lamp on or off as needed; this repeats continuously.
items.markingKey: 1 mark sensor; 1 mark actuator; 1 mark comparison with pre-set value; 1 mark actuator switched / continuous loop [4]

items.stem: A greenhouse owned by Palm Grove Hotel near Nairobi grows tropical plants that need a temperature of 24 °C to 28 °C and moist soil. (a) State whether this is a monitoring or a control system, with a reason. (b) Name two actuators that could be used.
items.answer: (a) Control if actuators change conditions (greenhouse/museum); monitoring if only warnings are given (hospital). (b) Heater, motor (window), water valve/pump, fan, dehumidifier.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark choice; 1 mark reason [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: What is an actuator?
options: A device that carries out a physical action on a signal from the computer
A type of input device such as a keyboard
items.answer: A device that carries out a physical action on a signal from the computer
items.markingKey: Actuators: motors, valves, relays, pumps, heaters.

items.stem: A bank in Lagos uses a computer system with sensors. Explain why a monitoring system may give a warning but not change anything.
items.answer: It has no actuators; it only records readings and alerts a human when values are outside limits.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Why is an analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) needed in a control system?
options: To amplify the output to actuators
Sensors produce analogue signals but the computer processes digital data
items.answer: Sensors produce analogue signals but the computer processes digital data
items.markingKey: ADC converts the continuously varying sensor voltage into binary values.

items.stem: Explain how feedback is used in a central heating system to keep a room at 21 °C.
items.answer: The sensor measures the temperature; the processor compares it with 21 °C; if lower, the heater is switched on, if higher it is switched off; the change in temperature is measured again, so the output affects the next input.
items.markingKey: 1 mark sensor measures; 1 mark compared with set point; 1 mark heater switched; 1 mark loop repeated / output affects input [4]

items.stem: Explain why a range is often used instead of a single target value in a control system.
items.answer: If a single value is used the actuator would switch on and off very rapidly (hunting), causing wear; a small range (hysteresis) prevents this.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: rapid switching; 1 mark: wear/energy, range prevents it [2]

items.stem: An ADC uses 12 bits for each sensor reading. How many different values can it produce?

An automatic irrigation system for a farm near Bangkok keeps soil moisture between 30% and 40%. (a) Explain why an ADC is needed in this system. (b) Describe what would happen if the sensor became faulty and always gave a low reading.
items.answer: (a) The sensor produces a continuous analogue voltage; the microprocessor needs digital values. (b) The processor would keep the pump/valve on, overfilling/overwatering; feedback fails.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: What is feedback in a control system?

items.markingKey: Closed loop: the effect of the actuator is measured by the sensor and used for the next decision.

OR with a mask that has 0 in that position
items.answer: AND with a mask that has 0 in that bit position and 1 elsewhere
items.markingKey: AND with 0 clears the bit; AND with 1 keeps the others.

items.stem: Explain how a program can test whether a particular sensor flag is set in a status byte.
items.answer: AND the status byte with a mask that has 1 only in that bit position; if the result is non-zero (or equals the mask) the flag is set; then use CMP and a conditional jump.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: AND with mask; 1 mark: compare result/conditional jump [2]

items.stem: A heater in Pioneer Insurance is switched ON when the temperature is below 18 and OFF when it is above 22; otherwise it stays as it is. It starts OFF. For the readings 19, 25, 18, 22, 15, give the state of the heater after each reading.
items.answer: OFF, OFF, OFF, OFF, ON
items.markingKey: 19→OFF, 25→OFF, 18→OFF, 22→OFF, 15→ON. 1 mark per 2 correct states [3]

items.stem: An ADC uses 8 bits for each sensor reading. How many different values can it produce?
An ADC uses 6 bits for each sensor reading. How many different values can it produce? Explain the effect of using more bits.
items.answer: 64; more bits give more levels so a more accurate (higher resolution) reading
items.markingKey: 2^6 = 64 [1]; smaller step between levels / more accurate [1] [2]

items.stem: An automatic irrigation system for a farm near Singapore keeps soil moisture between 30% and 40%. (a) Explain why an ADC is needed in this system. (b) Describe how feedback is used to keep the value in range.
items.answer: (a) The sensor produces a continuous analogue voltage; the microprocessor needs digital values. (b) Sensor reading compared with limits; actuator switched on/off; resulting change measured again, affecting next decision.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [2] (b) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) A control byte uses one bit per device, where 1 means ON. Which operation switches one device ON without changing the others? (b) Which operation, with a suitable mask, switches one device OFF without changing the others?
items.answer: (a) OR with a mask that has 1 in that bit position (b) AND with a mask that has 0 in that bit position and 1 elsewhere
items.markingKey: (a) OR sets the bit; other bits ORed with 0 are unchanged. (b) AND with 0 clears the bit; AND with 1 keeps the others.

items.stem: Mohammed wants to switch OFF only the device controlled by bit 6 (bit 1 most significant) of the value 00000110, and uses AND #B00000100. Explain the problem and give the correct mask.
items.answer: AND with 00000100 clears every bit except bit 6, so all other devices are switched off. The mask should be 11111011 (0 in bit 6, 1 elsewhere), giving 00000010.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: explains other bits cleared; 1 mark: correct mask 11111011 [2]

items.stem: Grace wants to switch OFF only the device controlled by bit 2 (bit 1 most significant) of the value 00011011, and uses AND #B01000000. Explain the problem and give the correct mask.
items.answer: AND with 01000000 clears every bit except bit 2, so all other devices are switched off. The mask should be 10111111 (0 in bit 2, 1 elsewhere), giving 00011011.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: explains other bits cleared; 1 mark: correct mask 10111111 [2]

items.stem: A control register holds one bit per device (bit 1 motor, bit 2 fan, bit 3 lamp, bit 4 pump, bit 5 heater, bit 6 alarm, bit 7 buzzer, bit 8 valve; bit 1 is the most significant, 1 = ON). It currently holds 11110100. Give the bitwise operation and mask needed to switch the heater ON, and the resulting value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark operation OR; 1 mark mask 00001000; 1 mark result 11111100 [3]

items.stem: A greenhouse controller stores the states of four devices in the lower four bits of address 300 (bit 5 = buzzer, bit 6 = lamp, bit 7 = pump, bit 8 = alarm; bit 8 least significant; 1 = ON). Address 300 contains 00000100. (a) Write assembly code using LDD, OR, AND and STO to switch the pump ON and the lamp OFF. (b) Give the new contents of address 300. (c) Explain why masks are used rather than storing a new value directly.
items.answer: (a) LDD 300; OR #B00000010; AND #B11111011; STO 300 (b) 00000010 (c) only the chosen bits change; other devices keep their current state
